chunks: Ali narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man: does anything that passes in front of him cut off his salat (prayer)? He said: Nothing cuts off the salat (prayer) of a Muslim, but ward off whatever you can.

key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِ: the Muslim, meaning the person whose salat (prayer) is under discussion
key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ: in front of him, literally between his hands, meaning before the person praying
key_terms.صَلَاتَهُ: his salat (prayer), referring to the ritual prayer being performed
key_terms.لَا يَقْطَعُ: does not cut off or invalidate
key_terms.مَا اسْتَطَعْتَ: whatever you are able, to the extent possible
key_terms.يَمُرُّ: passes by, meaning something moving across the space before the worshipper

ai.seo_question: Does something passing in front of a person invalidate his salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that things passing in front of a person do not invalidate the salat (prayer) of a Muslim. At the same time, it instructs the worshipper to prevent such interruption as much as possible, indicating proper prayer etiquette without judging the prayer invalid.
